answer: In the PoA grove each agent stakes a unique quartz‑signed credential recorded as a beacon on the ledger, binding the identity to a verifiable hardware root. Quadratic weighting then aggregates reputation so that the influence of n low‑stake identities grows as √n, while a single well‑staked node contributes linearly, making many fake accounts cheap but powerless. An attacker must acquire a comparable quartz token for each genuine‑looking node, driving cost roughly linear with desired influence and rendering a Sybil flood economically prohibitive.
